transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I feel like I’ve ruined everything in my life and I don’t deserve to be doing art or working with anyone anymore. Everything just feels completely broken, and I don't even know how to begin fixing it.
Have you had other times in your life when you felt depressed like this for at least two weeks, or is this the first episode? Did this start after a specific stressful event or major loss?

This is the first time I've ever experienced depression like this. It started about two years ago and has been steadily building since my contentious divorce, which completely upended my marriage and my plans for museum work.

Since the divorce, have your symptoms stayed tied mainly to that stressor, or have they become a more constant depression that affects you most days even when you’re not thinking about it? How much has this been interfering with your work, relationships, or basic daily activities?

The depression has become a constant, heavy weight that is there every single day, far beyond just thinking about the divorce. Because of it, I've completely stopped working, fallen behind on my rent, and let all my friendships and soccer groups slip away. I'm just too ashamed and overwhelmed to show up to anything anymore.
Have you had thoughts of wanting to die, hurt yourself, or end your life? If so, have you made any plans or taken any steps toward it?

Yes, a few times a week I catch myself thinking it would be better for everyone if I just didn't wake up. On really dark nights, I've Googled painless ways to die and imagined how I'd do it, but I get scared and close my laptop before actually making a plan or taking any steps.

Even on days when something good happens or you’re distracted, does your mood lift at all, or do you still feel depressed nearly all day? And does it still feel mainly tied to the divorce, or has it taken on a life of its own?

No, my mood doesn't lift at all; that heavy, gray feeling stays with me all day, and I don't get any joy out of anything anymore even if I try to distract myself. While it all started after the painful divorce, it definitely feels like the depression has taken on a life of its own now and is constantly dragging me down.

Have you ever heard or seen things that others couldn’t, or felt certain of something like being guilty, ruined, or deserving punishment even when others told you it wasn’t true? If yes, did that happen only when you were feeling this depressed?

Yes, I hear a harsh male voice telling me I'm a fraud who should disappear, and I'm convinced my old friends are blacklisting me online because I feel so guilty and ruined. But it doesn't only happen when I'm depressed; last summer, even when my mood lifted for a few weeks and I felt okay, I still heard that voice and believed the blacklisting was real.

During that period last summer when your mood felt okay, for about how long did the voice and the blacklisting belief continue while you were not depressed at all? Were they present for at least two weeks on their own?

Yes, they were definitely present on their own for at least two or three weeks. Even though my mood had lifted and I didn't feel especially sad or numb during that time, the voice at night and the belief that people were blacklisting me continued without stopping.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a prolonged major depressive syndrome with severe functional impairment and suicidality, together with persistent psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and delusional/paranoid guilt-blacklisting beliefs). Crucially, psychotic symptoms also persisted for at least 2–3 weeks during a period when mood symptoms had lifted, which supports schizoaffective disorder, depressive type, rather than major depressive disorder with psychotic symptoms or an adjustment disorder.
